en: Lightning can and does strike the same place many times; the Empire State Building in New York is struck by lightning about 25 times every year.
Earth's seasons are caused by its 23.5-degree axial tilt, not by Earth being closer to or farther from the Sun during its orbit.
Every part of the Moon receives sunlight during its orbit, so the so-called dark side is really just the far side we cannot see from Earth.
The Sun is not a ball of fire; it produces energy through nuclear fusion, which converts hydrogen atoms into helium atoms in its extremely hot core.
Soil is not just broken rock; it is a mixture of weathered rock, minerals, decomposed organic matter called humus, water, and air.
Cumulonimbus clouds are not white and fluffy; they are dark, towering clouds that produce heavy rain, thunderstorms, hail, and even tornadoes.
A star's apparent brightness depends on both its distance from Earth and its actual luminosity, which is the total amount of energy it emits.
Earthquakes happen when tectonic plates get stuck at their edges and then suddenly release years of built-up stress energy along a fault line.
The water cycle never ends when rain falls; water then evaporates from surfaces, transpires from plants, and rises back into the atmosphere to repeat the cycle.
Pluto is not a planet; the International Astronomical Union reclassified it as a dwarf planet in 2006 because it has not cleared its orbital neighborhood.
Although diamonds rank 10 on the Mohs hardness scale, they can still be scratched by other diamonds and can shatter if struck with a hammer.
Tornadoes and hurricanes are not the same; tornadoes form over land from thunderstorms and are small, while hurricanes form over warm oceans and span hundreds of miles.
